In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
echocardiographic abnormalities are common in neurologically ill patients and the prevalence increases with age.

in patients referred from neurological departments, echocardiography is indicated to assess cardiac function in the presence of heart failure, arrhythmia and/or endocarditis and in the presence of a history of stroke, especially in patients ≥66 years of age, in order to exclude or establish LVHT and left ventricular thrombi.
echocardiographic abnormalities are frequently found in patients referred from a neurological ward.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in patients referred for echocardiographic examination from the neurological department, a comprehensive echocardiographic evaluation is mandatory, since the prevalence of abnormalities is high.
the most frequent echocardiographic abnormalities detected in patients from a neurologic clinic are impaired relaxation, left ventricular wall thickness and valvular abnormalities.
in neurologically ill patients, the prevalence of LVHT and thrombus is low.
The main takeaway from our work is that
echocardiographers should be aware of the possibility of LVHT in patients from a neurology department.
LVHT is a rare finding in neurologically ill patients.
the echocardiographic examination of neurology patients should be performed by an expert cardiologist, who can recognize the abnormalities and make the right diagnosis.
